_comment: Curated food library for the Nutrition workspace. Synced into the `foods` table on startup by scoring/foodlib.py.
All macros are PER 100 GRAMS - that is how nutrition data is published, and it is the only basis on which recipes compose.
serving_grams is one typical portion, offered as a convenience so nobody has to weigh a banana. Grams remain the stored unit.
Values are rounded reference figures for common preparations, not a clinical database. Where raw and cooked differ materially
(rice, pasta, oats, lentils) the cooked form is listed, because that is what ends up on the plate and in the log.
One food per line, deliberately: it keeps the file reviewable as a diff.
Removing an entry archives it rather than deleting - someone may have logged a meal against it.
Alcohol is the one place kcal does not reconcile with 4/4/9: ethanol carries 7 kcal/g and is not a macronutrient.
wine-red and spirits are therefore correct as written, and the library test exempts them rather than treating it as an error.

`unit` is a DISPLAY unit: storage and every nutrition calculation stay in grams. Liquids read in ml because nobody knows how many grams of coffee they drank. Oils keep grams - they are about 0.92 g/ml and measured by the spoon, so ml would quietly misstate them by 8%.
